item.title: Apple, Tata to probe deaths of three workers at iPhone parts factory in Tamil Nadu: What we know so far
item.description: A fatal gas inhalation incident at Tata Electronics’ iPhone-components factory in Tamil Nadu killed three contract workers inspecting a tank. Nalco Water said the workers were employed by a subcontractor and pledged to cooperate with authorities. Apple and Tata have also launched investigations.
item.dc:creator: Livemint
item.content:encoded: A day after three contract workers were killed at Tata Electronics’ iPhone components factory in Tamil Nadu, Apple has reportedly sent a team to investigate the deaths.The deaths, which occurred late on Monday, will be investigated by Apple, Tata and the state authorities, state officials and two industry sources with direct knowledge told Reuters.Three workers die at Tata's iPhone factory: What we know so farThree contract workers died during water tank maintenance work at the Tata Electronics factory that makes parts for Apple iPhones in Tamil Nadu on Monday.What led to their death? The three contract workers died during maintenance work on an effluent treatment plant operated by Nalco Water at the Tata facility in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, district official Dinesh Kumar said.He added that the deaths occurred when the workers inhaled gas while inspecting an external nano-filtration tank.“Three worker deaths at Tata Apple iPhone parts factory occurred due to asphyxiation,” a source told Reuters.Workers hired by sub-contractors: Nalco Water, which is part of US-headquartered Ecolab, said in a statement, according to Reuters, that the three workers were engaged by one of its sub-contractors and that the incident occurred in a utility facility it operates.The company said it was working with local authorities in the investigation. "We take this incident extremely seriously," Nalco Water said.Probe launched: "Tamil Nadu minister Virudhai Magal Keerthana said in a post on X that the worker deaths will be 'thoroughly investigated and appropriate action will be taken based on the findings."There has been no impact on production as the facility was closed for the Hindu festival of Deepavali this week, the two industry sources told Reuters, adding that Tata and Apple will both investigate the incident.“Tata will investigate the deaths at its iPhone parts factory; teams were on site overnight,” the source said on Tuesday, a day after the incident.Meanwhile, Apple's team is visiting the plant to assist in the ongoing investigation, one of the sources said.The salt-to-aviation Tata Group's electronics unit accounts for roughly 40 percebnt of iPhone assembly and Foxconn makes up the rest in India.Tata has in recent months faced many challenges as its iPhone-making operations have been hit by a ransomware attack and concerns of water pollution.Over the years, as Apple expanded manufacturing beyond China, India has emerged as a key hub which now accounts for roughly 25% of the world's iPhones.The three contract workers died during maintenance work on an effluent treatment plant at the facility which is located in Hosur in Tamil Nadu, district official Dinesh Kumar said.The effluent treatment plant was operated by Nalco Water, which is part of U.S.-headquartered Ecolab, he said, adding that the deaths occurred when the workers inhaled gas while inspecting an external nano-filtration tank.Tata Electronics, Apple and Nalco Water did not respond to Reuters requests for comment.Tamil Nadu is a key industrial hub in India, hosting factories of many global giants like Foxconn, Hyundai, VinFast and BMW.Tata's Hosur site has faced repeated setbacks: a fire halted production at the components plant in 2024, and state authorities warned of a shutdown over alleged groundwater contamination this year before dropping the matter.Separately, a ransomware breach at an adjacent iPhone plant, located in the same compound, leaked documents linked to Apple's then-unreleased iPhone 18 Pro, Reuters has reported.

item.title: China’s trade surplus tops $1 trn for second year in a row, exports jump 35.2% in October: What's leading the surge?
item.description: China's trade surplus crossed $1 trillion in the first 10 months of 2026, driven by strong demand for AI-related products and high-tech exports. However, weak domestic consumption and growing trade tensions with the US and EU pose fresh challenges for Beijing.
item.dc:creator: Swati Gandhi
item.content:encoded: As US President Donald Trump is likely to meet his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping, for the third time this year at next week's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, Beijing's trade surplus has soared past $1 trillion in the first 10 months of 2026.The data comes amid a global race to build artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, which has driven demand for high-tech products and boosted exports, helping offset weak domestic demand. The trend could further strain trade relations with major partners, Reuters reported.China’s exports soar past $1 trillion: What's leading the surge?In October, exports jumped 35.2% compared with the same month last year in US dollar terms, according to customs data released on Tuesday (local time). The increase was slightly below September's 36.3% growth but exceeded economists' expectations of a 33.5% rise. This helped push Beijing's cumulative trade surplus to $1.04 trillion in the first 10 months of 2026, crossing the $1 trillion mark for a second consecutive year and reaching the milestone a month earlier than in 2025.China's exports stood at $412.3 billion in October, while imports totalled $307.1 billion. The monthly trade surplus, however, narrowed to $105.3 billion from $133.5 billion in September as imports grew at a faster pace.China's imports recorded a 41.6% year-on-year increase in October, surpassing the 32% growth projected by economists surveyed by Reuters. The rise also marked an acceleration from the 31% increase reported in September.The data highlights Beijing's increasing dependence on exports to sustain economic growth amid weak consumer spending and a prolonged downturn in the property sector. Although strong global investment in AI is likely to support demand for Chinese technology goods through 2027, analysts caution that greater reliance on foreign markets could expose the country to rising trade barriers while concealing underlying domestic economic challenges.Customs data also showed that rare earth exports edged higher from September, while crude oil imports jumped to their highest level since March as buyers adjusted to supply disruptions in the Middle East.US-China trade dataAccording to the report, China's trade surplus with the United States narrowed marginally from $34.01 billion in September to $32.71 billion in October, though the broader imbalance between the world's two largest economies continues to be a source of friction.Earlier on Monday, Beijing and Washington formally extended their trade truce until January 10, 2027, giving both sides additional time to work towards a broader trade understanding.China's exports to create friction with the European Union?The growing trade surplus may fuel further tensions with the European Union, where leaders have sought additional trade restrictions on China. This comes after Beijing and the bloc reached an agreement to curb Chinese exports of hybrid vehicles to the European market over the next few years.However, as the new measures are not yet in force, manufacturers are likely to accelerate shipments ahead of their implementation, providing a short-term boost to exports.(with inputs from Reuters)
